answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small deposit that only unlocks after a long horizon of honest participation, so creating thousands of fake accounts becomes expensive. New identities enter through a single narrow inlet - a verified sponsor or a proof-of-work gate - rather than opening freely at dawn of every epoch. Because the stake is slashed on fraud and returned only after sustained good behavior, attackers pay real cost per identity while honest agents keep working.
